summary.headline: Manba Finance Q4 FY26: PAT up 39% YoY to INR 11 crore; FY26 AUM INR 1,713 crore, up 29% YoY, with NIM at 13.63%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net interest income of INR 50 crore (up 34% YoY) and PAT of INR 11 crore (up 39% YoY). For FY26, NII rose 24% to INR 162 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR 45 crore, with ROE at 11.65% and ROA at 2.63%. Asset quality improved slightly QoQ, with gross Stage-3 at 3.33% and net at 2.46%, and the company raised its provision coverage. Management guided to 25-30% AUM growth, with new products (MSME LAP, used car, 3-Wheeler) and geographies (Karnataka, UP, MP) being added.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 842 crore a year earlier
GNPA from 3.38% in Dec 2025; NNPA from 2.57%

segments.name: Product mix (AUM)
segments.commentary: 2-Wheeler 84.5%, small business loan 4.93%, top-up loan 4.70%, 3-Wheeler 3.28%, used vehicle loan 1.50%. 2-Wheeler was about 97% three years ago; target is about 65% in three years.

segments.name: Portfolio split by channel
segments.commentary: MFL business 91.84%, DA and BC 4.43%, co-lending 2.62%, and 1.11% in the remaining category.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Maharashtra share of customer onboarding fell from about 58% to about 40%; Gujarat about 27% and Rajasthan about 15%. 130 locations across 6 states.

guidance_outlook: AUM guidance of INR 2,300-2,400 crore by year-end, implying 25-30% growth, with 30% incremental growth targeted.
Karnataka launch planned for Q2 FY27; West Bengal considered by end of FY27 or later. Nashik and Ahmedabad MSME LAP branches planned next quarter.
Borrowing cost currently about 10.50%, down from about 11.25%; management says it will not borrow above 10.50% and is seeking a further 20-50 bps reduction.
Equity fundraise now expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 (earlier target Q2 or Q3), possibly deferred 3-4 months due to geopolitical conditions; comfort debt-to-equity below 4x.
Management said it will target 60-65% 2-Wheeler share of the book within three years.
capex_capacity: MSME LAP launched with two branches (Mumbai and Pune); ticket size INR 5-20 lakh, LTV up to 60%, gross yield 18-19%.
Dealer network expanded to about 1,650 from about 1,200, with about 200 added in the last two quarters, mainly used 2-Wheeler; used 2-Wheeler presence is about 150 dealerships.
Around 900+ sales staff out of about 1,800 employees; customer base over 2.20 lakh live customers after adding about 28,500 in the quarter.
Expansion focus on UP (about 1% market share) and MP (about 3% market share).
demand_pricing: Disbursement growth about 16% YoY, driven by 2-Wheeler demand and dealer expansion; 2-Wheeler grew about 14% in April per management.
Used 2-Wheeler ticket INR 55-60k with first-year performance described as promising; new 2-Wheeler ticket INR 80-85k.
New geographies lent at 18-19% versus 21-22% in established markets to attract stronger borrowers.

EV 2-Wheeler about 7-8% of industry; company's EV exposure is similar, with 3-Wheeler EV about INR 40 crore of a roughly INR 50 crore 3-Wheeler book. Management says EV 2-Wheeler NPA is about 1% after 3.5 years.
Small business loan growth is being slowed because of tighter credit policy and a weak demand environment; it is under 5% of AUM.
TVS Motor all-India MOU has helped onboard about 70 TVS 3-Wheeler dealers in three months, with subvention and credit-loss support from TVS.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected 2-Wheeler vs other product mix and new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: 2-Wheeler share to fall to about 65% in three years from about 84% now; Karnataka starts in Q2 and UP and MP are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable AUM growth rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is 25-30% growth per year; AUM expected at INR 2,300-2,400 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provision coverage rise from 24% to 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is to strengthen the balance sheet against Stage-3 assets and possible calamities, given strong profitability. Credit loss was about 1.12-1.25% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Current incremental cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about 10.50%, down from about 11.25% a year earlier; PTC deal at about 9.75% and an SBI sanction of INR 100 crore at about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Early signs of stress from fuel prices and the vehicle book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not much so far: 100-125cc bikes, EMI INR 3,500-4,000, 20-25% down payment. Small business loans are seeing tighter policy and higher rejections.

qa_highlights.question: Equity fundraise timing and valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeted Q2 or Q3 FY27, now possibly Q3 or Q4; shares traded around INR 140-150 in February and the company may wait for INR 135-150.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and fuel-price pressure on the vehicle book; management reports no stress yet but has tightened small business loan underwriting.
3-Wheeler EV and used-vehicle collection risk; management called 3-Wheeler collection very challenging, and 3-Wheeler yields and losses need monitoring.
Dependence on 2-Wheeler (about 84.5% of AUM); the shift in mix is planned but not yet visible.
Equity fundraise timing and dilution risk, which may be deferred 3-4 months depending on market conditions.
New-geography collection build-out in UP, MP and Karnataka, where lower yields are being used to manage risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with specific numbers offered throughout. Cautious on the macro backdrop (geopolitical risk, fuel prices) and on the equity raise timing. Some answers were unclear or corrected on the floor, including on the cost-of-borrowing and credit-loss figures.
key_quotes: Our credit loss is around 1% to 1.25% only across the year at the AUM of INR 100 crores and at INR AUM 1700 crores also.
So, we are not very much focused on the small business loan because that is the only unsecured product company is having and, of course, the outer limit of the AUM is only less than 5%.

adds.what: MSME LAP branches in Nashik and Ahmedabad (planned)
Dealer network expanded to about 1,650 from about 1,200 (about 200 added in last two quarters)

growth.why: Guidance of 25-30% AUM growth (INR 2,300-2,400 cr by year-end, midpoint ~27.5%) is backed by disbursements up ~16% YoY, dealer network expansion to ~1,650, 2-Wheeler growth ~14% in April and new MSME LAP, used vehicle and Karnataka/UP/MP launches, but no specific capacity or order-book numbers are quantified.
